summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This conversation documents Session 80 of an ongoing computational physics project called LOWDIN, in which Claude operates as a persistent research instrument across sessions using a structured handoff protocol. The person opened the session by ruling on scope: items 1, 2, and 3 from the prior session's proposed agenda should be executed in order, with item 3 (a second atomic number comparison) retained on the basis that it might prove useful even if its value was uncertain in advance.

The project involves Hartree-Fock self-consistent field calculations for heavy atoms, tracking which electronic configuration (the "entrant") wins at each atomic number Z by total energy difference. Session 80 addressed two completed items and did not reach the third due to context limits. Item 1 repaired a currency fault (F79.2) in which f-channel orbital energies had been compared against total-energy differences—mismatched quantities. The repair required building a node-targeted fallback instrument (de80.py) that returns target-node states to the SCF rather than raising exceptions, enabling total energies to be computed and differenced against a sealed reference of −25694.384010 Ha. The Z=89 table was restated: 6f/7f/8f came in at −20.486, −14.282, and −10.528 mHa respectively, all well above both rank-1 (6d, −157.620 mHa) and rank-2 (7p, −125.288 mHa), with margins now expressed as ratios of like quantities. Item 2 ran the first-ever perturbation falsifier for an adopted global-minimizer rule (O-C1), perturbing converged Z=89 orbitals and re-converging across ten configurations in two perturbation kinds and four amplitudes. No second basin was resolved; all eight converged runs agreed to 1.7 parts per billion, establishing a sensitivity floor of approximately 0.035 mHa rather than proving global minimality.

Three faults were raised and documented against this session's own work. F80.1 diagnosed an unresolved prior anomaly: two zeros carry the target node count in the f-channel scan, and two instruments silently selected opposite members based solely on argument order in their respective geomspace calls, with neither declaring an orientation. Running both revealed that the more-bound branch supports no self-consistent field at any of the three channels, while the less-bound branch converges at all three; prior f-channel eigenvalues were withdrawn as descriptions of SCF states. F80.2 was discovered when a zero-perturbation control check failed: the sealed energies sit approximately 0.034 mHa above their own basin floor because the SCF stopping criterion operates on eigenvalue drift while the adopted rule is stated on total energy. F80.3 was raised against the session's own comparator tolerance, which was set below the resolution F80.2 measured, causing the instrument to label ordinary convergence scatter as falsifying results; those labels were overridden in the result record with the reason attached. The session sealed at 1310/1310 files after a fresh-extract test caught a tar construction error (missing root-level files) that was corrected before final handoff. Item 3 (fixed-field comparison at Z=90) carries forward to Session 81 as item 1, now inheriting three repairs the prior session lacked.

| canary | **CLEAN** — float, kernel, numpy, physics |

Project knowledge reviewed first (Method 1.6 corpus + code/coordinates). S79-RECORD.md read in full, all 449 lines, no truncation carried forward.

---

## THE STANDING POSITION, AS S79 LEFT IT

**Held:** the fixed-field inequality is computed at Z=89 — eps₃^{l=3} − eps₄^{l=2} = **+155.369 mHa** in one field, with relaxation measured at **10.072 mHa and closing the gap**. That is a measurement, not a derivation, and s79 says so in its own text.

**Open, and owed against a written result:** **F79.2**. The Z=89 margin table compares one-electron eigenvalues against total-energy differences. Measured offset at 6d is 19.277 mHa against a margin of 32.330 mHa. Every stated *multiple of the margin* is withdrawn; the qualitative verdict survives provisionally on a one-channel offset estimate that is not a bound.

---

## RECONNAISSANCE FOR ITEM 1 — DONE BEFORE ASKING FOR THE RULING

The repair is buildable. `t7e_probe.make_shoot` returns `u` as well as `nd`/`nrm`, so a node-targeted fallback can return solve_one's full contract rather than raising as `refine79` does. The five sealed Z=89 failures are all RuntimeError node-count raises at 3–4 s each, so a converged run is minutes, not hours.

**One hazard I want on the record before anything is built:** `refine79`'s scan bounds are hardcoded from the s77 windows, which describe the field at *one* iteration. A fallback living inside a live SCF sees the field move under it every iteration. An instrument that reports "no zero at target node count" when its own scan bound was too narrow is exactly F79.1's shape — and s79 already caught that once, in code written that session, only because a prediction was filed first. The scan bound must be adaptive and declared, and the prediction must say what it expects before the bound is chosen.

---

## AWAITING YOUR RULING — SCOPE FOR S80

The s79 order proposes, in order:

1. **F79.2's currency repair** — Z=89 SCF at cfg+6f/7f/8f with node-targeted fallback, report dE against −25694.384010, then restate the item-2 margins in dE. Owed against a result already written down.
2. **O-C1's falsifier** — perturb a converged Z=89 6d solution, re-converge. Cheap, never run, load-bearing since Step 0(ii) was adopted.
3. **Fixed-field comparison at a second row**, Z=90 the strongest candidate.

My recommendation is **1, then 2** — item 1 because a withdrawn claim sitting in the record is the most expensive thing here, item 2 because it is cheap and currently the only thing standing between a four-start basin test and a claim the adopted rule cannot support.

Item 3 buys a second Z but does not close anything already owed.

Your ruling on scope, and I file the prediction before any run.

### 2.24 Never one heuristic — §2.8, and the one thing it does not say

    Where a quantity is reached by a heuristic rather than computed, run at least two
    heuristics of different kind and **report the SPREAD**. A single heuristic cannot
    tell you whether it is in the case where it works.

 **The first sentence is §2.8 and this book already had it.** *For every quantity that matters, build
 a second derivation that does not pass through the first* — and the seed is a quantity that matters,
 prune-greedy was one derivation, and no second was ever built. **§2.8's own gloss is what happened:
 an identity computed along one path is vacuous.** The protocol was not missing; it was not applied.

 **What §2.24 adds is the SPREAD.** §2.8 asks for agreement between two routes and is satisfied when
 they agree. **A spread of thirty-three around an exact seven is not disagreement about a value — it
 is information about which case you are in**, and §2.8 has no place to put it. That is the whole of
 what is new here.

 *Found by indexing the protocols: §2.8 and §2.24 occupy the same cell in every coordinate — trigger,
 object, failure and how each was earned. Register 514.*

 **This protocol exists because that failure ran for twelve cycles.** Every seed size in §14.5.7 and
 §14.5.8 came from one algorithm — prune-greedy — and every expression fitted to those sizes was
 checked against numbers from the same source. **The fits could not fail**, which is §4.6's condition
 for a check that is not evidence.

 **What the spread shows.** Five heuristics on Λ₈ give 12, 7, 7, 7 and **40**, around an exact seven.
 On a regular down-set they give 7, 7, 7, 7, 7 — and the lower bound is 7 too, so the answer is
 exact. **The spread is zero where the object is regular and thirty-three where it is not**, and no
 single run distinguishes those cases.

    **A heuristic's output is a bound. Two heuristics' outputs are a bound and a
    warning. Neither is a value.**

 And a lower bound is worth as much as a second heuristic: §14.5.9's disjoint-witness bound is what
 showed the gap between seven and forty was real rather than a tie. Register 506.

### 3.1 Why three of the audits were needed
 CONSISTENCY: twenty-eight cross-references once pointed at a section that had moved. ARTEFACT: a
 rendered page once carried glyphs the source did not. ATTRIBUTION: the three precedents that place
 this book's central theorem in existing literature were cited in the text and absent from the
 References. Each history is in the register — 262, 285, 294 and the grouped mechanisms at §28.7.8.
 **A protocol states what to do; the record states what happened.**

### 3.2 The whitespace clause, and two measurements that were wrong
 A gap a reader sees is a defect the source cannot show.

The Method 1.6-1.md
** E falls as a fibration is refined and rises as
 coordinates are added, because both are acts of realisation — choosing a fibration realises a
 partition, adding a coordinate realises a distinction. **A zero is worth the size of the box it was
 computed in** because the box is the realisation. That entry stated the fact; this law states why.

 **The law distinguishes two ways of realising, and the difference is measurable.** Λ closes through
 its own *order* — the constraint tree of monotone single-variable bounds is ℛ — and the closure is
 total, E(X) = 0 with nothing left over. Maxwell's equations close through an internal *identity*:
 pre-1861 Ampère's law contains its own contradiction, since ∇·(∇×H) = 0 forces ∇·J = 0, which fails
 whenever charge density varies; the repair is compelled, and the identity ∇·∇× = 0 is what realises
 the closure. Both satisfy *realised in the object's own structure*. **They do not deliver the same
 thing.** Identity-realisation closed only the divergence part and left any additional curl free —
 genuine slack, closed later and externally by covariance.

    **Conjecture (slack = kernel).** Identity-realised closure leaves slack equal to the kernel of
    the realising identity; order-realised closure leaves none.

 Two computed points: ∇·∇× has an enormous kernel — every curl — and Maxwell's slack was exactly a
 curl; the rectangular cavity's admissible core closes by μ = ν − 1, whose kernel is trivial, and its
 slack was zero. **Two points are not a pattern**, and it is stated sharply enough to be attacked; if
 it holds, the law gains a computable correction term rather than a qualitative clause, which is what
 §1 requires before anything joins the formalised principles.

 **And a criterion falls out of the same work, in a form that needed correcting one turn after it was
 retained.** As first stated: *an occupancy coordinate is admissible if and only if its cap is a
 function of a single other coordinate.* The forward direction holds and the *only if* is false. A cap
 of two arguments closes meets perfectly well provided it is a **meet-morphism** — bond order capped
 by min(v_A, v_B) is two-argument and fails nothing. Computed over six cap forms:

  cap                          join failures   meet failures   meet-morphism   join-morphism
  φ(a) = a, single, increasing            0               0        yes             yes
  φ(a) = 4 − a, single, decreasing      875               0        no              no
  φ = min(a, b)                           0               0        yes             no
  φ = max(a, b)                           0             260        no              yes
  φ = (a>0) + (b>0)                       0              16        no              no
  φ = a + b                               0             400        no              no

    **Meets survive exactly when the cap is a meet-morphism; joins survive exactly when it is a
    join-morphism.

The Method 1.6-1.md
** Ne II fails at D = 5 with two shells; Ar II succeeds at D = 5 with three; Bi I succeeds at D = 5 with five.

### 2.5 Census before search
    Compute which species could work before looking for data.

 D is obtained from the core configuration by enumerating antisymmetric states. No spectroscopic data enters. **27 sequences admitted, 12 needing exceptional depth, 5 excluded structurally.**

### 2.6 Declines are recorded
    A collection reporting only successes cannot be checked.

 Every species examined and rejected is listed with its cause. Four causes have been identified — dilution, depth, coupling-scheme change, and core-excited interleaving — and §23.11 gives a worked case of each.

### 2.7 Exhaustive verification where possible

    Sampling n cells with no failure bounds the failure rate at ρ ≤ 3/n at 95% confidence. It
    never certifies ρ = 0.

 Where a claim is universally quantified over a finite lattice, it is checked on **every** cell. Where sampling is used, the sample size is stated.

### 2.8 Two independent routes
    For every quantity that matters, build a second derivation that does not pass through the
    first.

 This is ⅅ_def made operational. It caught a mis-stated relation in Chapter 16, and it is realised
 experimentally in the antiprotonic-helium check of §16.4, where two laser measurements agree at 0.09σ
 with no shared step.

 **An identity computed along one path is vacuous.** *w* = *V*·*e* cannot fail if *V* is *defined* as *w*/*e*.

### 2.9 Refuse rather than coerce
    No third state. A quantity is admissible or it is refused; it is never silently defaulted.

 A guard returning a null that a caller coerces to a Boolean produced three false conclusions in this work, none of which looked wrong. **Totality is the only mechanism that catches this**, and it works by preventing the computation rather than by detecting the error.

### 2.10 Retrieval
    Enumerate targets from the index before searching. List routes per cell. Prefer high-ρ
    cells. Read every retrieved source for its successors. When a route is blocked, move
    along the route set. Record ρ for cells that fail. And RE-ENUMERATE whenever the set the
    targets are drawn from grows.

 Chapter 19. A blocked cell with ρ = 1 is a **stated gap**, not an unexplained absence.

 The second clause was added late. §30.4 found five enumerations in one chapter — its own target list,
 §30.2's structural invariants, and the object lists of §31.1, §31.2 and §31.3 — each made once, against
 a structure that kept growing. Every one of them was incomplete when re-run.

    Enumerating once is not a protocol. It is a snapshot, and a snapshot of a growing object
    is a defect the moment it is taken.

### 2.11 Provenance
    Every number traces to a compilation, table and page, or to a database entry with its
    stated uncertainty.

 Appendix B carries this at channel level for all 153 channels.

The Method 1.6 — The Register-1.md
The literature's own universal structure answers it.* **The extended corner symmetry algebra is g_S = (diff(S) ⊕ sl(2,ℝ)^S) ⊕ (ℝ²)^S — Freidel, Oliveri, Pranzetti & Speziale JHEP 09 (2021) 083; Ciambelli & Leigh arXiv 2207.06441 — and its three factors sort cleanly by locality. sl(2,ℝ)^S, the surface BOOSTS, is described in the sources as the space of FUNCTIONS from the corner to SL(2,ℝ): one copy per point, ULTRALOCAL. (ℝ²)^S, the surface TRANSLATIONS: one copy per point, ULTRALOCAL. And diff(S), the surface DIFFEOMORPHISMS: vector fields whose bracket carries a derivative, which COUPLES neighbouring points. Exactly one factor of three is non-ultralocal.** *And Chandrasekaran and Flanagan's corner modes are the other two. Their own words are 'relative BOOSTS and null TRANSLATIONS of the respective corners' — sl(2,ℝ)^S and (ℝ²)^S, both ultralocal. diff(S) does not enter the construction.* **So the coupling mechanism exists, is named, is universal, and is ABSENT from the edge-mode construction M.C2 has rested on for four hundred entries. The semidirect product says how it would act: Diff(S) ⋉ SL(2,ℝ)^S means a diffeomorphism CARRIES a(y) TO a(φ(y)), which is precisely the relation between distinct points that nothing else supplied.** *One inference beyond the sources, flagged as mine: if a(y) transforms under Diff(S) then its physical content is its DIFFEOMORPHISM CLASS, not the function — and a scalar on S modulo Diff(S) is fixed by its level-set structure, a far smaller space than an arbitrary positive function. If that holds, register 1485's 'underdetermined by a whole function's worth' is too pessimistic and must be corrected downward. That is the next thing to test, and it is the first candidate this session that was not predicted to fail.* WARNING: *The inference at the end of this entry is WITHDRAWN at register 1488. diff(S) carries NON-VANISHING NOETHER CHARGE — it is PHYSICAL, not a gauge redundancy — so one must not quotient by it, and register 1485's underdetermination stands. Everything else in this entry holds: diff(S) IS the coupling mechanism, it IS the one non-ultralocal factor, and it IS absent from Chandrasekaran and Flanagan's construction.*

### 1488

**THE QUOTIENT IS NOT AVAILABLE: diff(S) IS PHYSICAL, NOT GAUGE — SO THE COUPLING ORGANISES THE FREEDOM RATHER THAN REDUCING IT.** *Register 1487 inferred that if a(y) transforms under Diff(S) its physical content is its diffeomorphism class, which would have cut the freedom from a function to a finite-dimensional stratum. Tested, and the fork settles against it from sources already held.* **Ciambelli and Leigh on the universal corner algebra: it is 'the subset of diffeomorphisms that become PHYSICAL at corners — codimension-2 surfaces SUPPORTING NOETHER CHARGES'. And Freidel and collaborators, Edge modes of gravity I: 'we get a NON-VANISHING CHARGE only when ξ does not vanish on S, [so] the corner symmetry subalgebra due to diffeomorphisms is simply diff(S)'.

The Method 1.6-1.md
**Extrapolating toward the flattening is cheap; away from it is not.**

    Rule 1 is a rule about direction, and it holds on whichever axis carries the defect.

 **Measured on two sequences, holding out each member in turn.** The lithium-like neutral is predicted from its three ions at 11.1% error; the sodium-like neutral at 23.4%. **The tight ends — C IV and Si IV — come back at 1.8% and 2.5%.**

### 22.2.3 And one step beyond the fitted range costs more again
 A hold-out is bracketed by the points that remain. A genuine prediction is not. Tested on the
 sodium-like sequence with P V — a fifth member — held out entirely:

| fit form | predicted δ(P V) | true | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| δ = *a* + *b*/*Z* | 0.8189 | 0.7129 | **14.9%** |
| **δ = *a* + *b*/*Z* + *c*/*Z*²** | 0.7376 | 0.7129 | **3.47%** |
| δ·*Z* linear in *Z* | 0.7835 | 0.7129 | 9.9% |

 **Only the quadratic form is usable, and it costs 3.5% rather than the 2.1% a hold-out suggests** — a factor of 1.7 for stepping outside the fitted range.

 **This matters for §25.6** The Sc VI prediction has a second, independent route through its isoelectronic sequence, and **3.5% is the figure that route must carry** — not 2.1%, and not the 1.3% of pure interpolation.

### 22.2.4 Rule 1's second clause is not redundant
 Sc III 3d is interior in n within ℓ = 2, and including it inflates the median error by 3.2× — because it is the
 collapsed ground state rather than a sequence member.

 **The operational test is the defect.** Its δ departs from its neighbours' by 0.14 where they depart from each other by 0.008 — **a factor of 17.** A cell can be interior by index and outside the sequence in fact, and the defect says which.

### 22.2.5 Rule 4 at the edge of a channel
 The two-parameter Ritz form needs three neighbours to leave a residual, and a channel with exactly three
 members has an interior cell with only two.

 Why Rule 4a exists
 The constant-defect form takes the mean of the available defects. On a monotone channel
 that mean lies between them — and therefore on the wrong side of the last one.

 **Sc VI's ⁴S°*n*s channel is the case that forced the clause.** With δ(4s) = 1.0057 and δ(5s) = 0.9812, the constant form gives **δ̄ = 0.9934 — above δ(5s)**, which a decreasing channel forbids. The resulting estimate falls **outside the deductive bracket its own monotonicity implies** (§25.6).

    A rule that produces an estimate its own bracket excludes is not a rule about uncertainty.
    It is an error.

 **With two neighbours the Ritz form is exactly determined** — two equations, two unknowns, no residual and therefore no fitted σ — but it is *admissible*, and Rule 3's separation means the bracket carries the guarantee while the point estimate carries none.

 **One further case in this work:** the Kr I (²P°₁⁄₂) *n*p series — 5p, 6p, 7p, with 6p interior. Under the constant-defect form the cell returns an estimate in error by −70.9 cm⁻¹ against σ = 602, or **0.12σ**.

The Method 1.6-1.md
Register 434.

 **The table's own vocabulary, defined.** Four terms in the rows above are used to define the
 coordinates and were never themselves defined, which is the failure S1 exists to prevent. They are
 defined here.

    **terms(ℓᵏ)** — the multiset of LS terms (2S, 2L) of the configuration ℓᵏ, obtained by
    **microstate enumeration**: list every way of placing k electrons in the 2(2ℓ+1) spin-orbitals,
    accumulate (2M_L, 2M_S), and strip complete (2S, 2L) blocks from the largest M_L down until the
    list is empty. This is the standard construction and the origin Chapter 7 already cites for
    2S ≤ k.

    **f_max** — the cap on f under §7.4, **not** the cell's own f. The distinction is the whole of
    §12.11.5: the bound 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max has one parent and preserves the tree and the cylinder;
    the same bound written with the cell's f has two parents and breaks the factorisation by 3.5%.
    Writing f_max without defining it left the book's title resting on an undefined subscript.

    **φ̂(k)** — the monotone envelope of k ↦ max 2J over the parent shells admitted by the caps, so
    φ̂ = {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5} at §7.4's. **This is not §6.1's φ̂ᵢⱼ**, which is ℛ's pairwise envelope
    max{xᵢ : x ∈ X, xⱼ ≤ v}. Both are monotone envelopes and that is the whole of the resemblance;
    one takes two coordinate indices and the other takes an occupancy. The collision is recorded
    rather than renamed, because renaming a symbol used 213 times is a larger risk than naming the
    two senses once. Register 250.

 **Density, stated so it can be rechecked.** For each axis, over every cell of the stage below that
 the lattice admits, count the values of the new coordinate that exact vector coupling realises and
 divide by the values the admissible bound allows. Three of the six exact sets are not the obvious
 ones and the column cannot be reproduced without them: seniority at axis 10 means the terms *new*
 at occupancy v — terms(f^v) less terms(f^(v−2)) as multisets, not merely a term of spin 2S′
 existing at v; the core's J at axis 11 is restricted to terms carrying the cell's own multiplicity 2S,
 not to all terms of ℓᵏ; and the target spin at axis 9 is the spin set of f^g by microstate
 enumeration. Under that definition all six entries reproduce exactly — 63.7, 67.5, 44.7, 17.0, 31.4,
 64.4 — at the caps of §7.4 and cap-dependent as always. Every bound is §14.4-admissible; every stage is closed — exhaustively to
 Λ₁₀, by the §7.3 proof beyond it — and every stage projects exactly onto the one below.
 Independence is demonstrated, not assumed, at every axis: p²'s ¹S and ¹D share a cell below axis
 10 and split at v; p¹'s ²P shares a cell below axis 11 and splits at J_c; and every K > 0 cell splits
 at J. Each coordinate is a physical degree of freedom that no function of the coordinates below it
 can express — the same door through which every legitimate axis must enter, by Chapter 17's theorem.

The Method 1.6-1.md
**R* is the only import**, and it has the status of the definition of a centimetre.

### 32.5.2 And it generalises to every bracket in the book
 The three inputs are tabulated per channel, so the property is not special to Sc VI:

    Every bracket in this book is recomputable from this book. All 1,061.

 **A reader with these pages and no internet reproduces each of them.**

### 32.5.3 Which is what D3 asks for, made operational
 §16.5 states totality as every claim supported, cited, or marked open. That is a bibliographic condition.
 This is the computational one:

    the index says which cell is being predicted — the coordinates are ordinary integers, and
    Λ contains the cell the book says every number the prediction needs

 **Together they close.** The index supplies the *what*; the collection supplies the *how much*; **and the seven-line arithmetic between them is printed in §25.6.**

 The one thing neither supplies is whether the prediction is true. That is §16.3's ⅅ_phys and it
 requires a spectrometer — which is exactly the boundary this book has been drawing since
 Chapter 6.

### 32.6 The falsification tests, run
 A book that invites the reader to look for its breaks has done less than one that looks itself.
 The three conditions are tested here, on this text, with the results reported whether or not they are
 favourable.

 Condition 1 — E(book) > 0
 A claim whose support the structure implies and the text omits.

 **Test.** Extract every chapter heading, every cross-reference, every section reference and every figure. Check that each target exists and that figures and captions pair.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| chapters cross-referenced but absent | **none** |
| § references to absent chapters | **none** |
| figures embedded / captions | 18 / 18 |
| **chapter numbering against the contents** | **FAILED** |

    The test found a break. This chapter was written as Chapter 31 while the contents listed it as 21,
    and Chapter 30 did not exist. E(book) was greater than zero: the structure implied a chapter the text
    did not carry.

 **It has been corrected**, and it is recorded here rather than silently repaired, because a falsification test that finds something and does not say so is worse than none.

 Condition 2 — D = 0 for some claim
 A claim carried without a verification count, so that an error in it would be undetectable.

 **Test.** Take every paragraph carrying a quantitative claim, excluding tables and citations, and check whether a verification appears within it.

| pass | claims | carrying a verification | bare |
|---|---|---|---|
| first run, same-line window | 85 | 46 (54%) | **39** |
| **corrected checker, paragraph window** | 63 | 56 (89%) | 7 |
| **after repair** | **63** | **60 (95%)** | **3** |

    The first run failed, and the failure was informative twice over.

The Method 1.6-1.md
That bound has **two parents**, which breaks the tree; §A.15 and register 230 record what
 it costs, 2,475 cells of the cylinder. The book substitutes f_max, the cap, giving one parent and a
 surviving factorisation. **The law is not abandoned but weakened**, and 39,375 of Λ₁₂'s 70,905 cells
 sit at an f below the cap, so for those the bound admits more than the law does. Dimension 13 inherits
 the weakening through K without adding to it.

 **φ̂ is not derived; it is observed.** Computed here: φ̂ = {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5}, and the largest 2J
 actually realised at each occupancy is {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5}. They are the same numbers because φ̂ *is*
 the envelope of the set's own extent. Λ₉ and Λ₁₀ take their bounds from laws that exist independently
 of Λ; Λ₁₁ takes its bound from Λ.

    **A bound taken from the law closes exactly. A bound taken from the extent closes only to an
    envelope.**

 That is why exactness is lost at the eleventh axis and not before it, and it is the same rule §15
 states for brackets: presume the next bracket from the law that generates the widths, never from the
 pattern the widths make.

 **And it says what E(X) measures.** ℛ builds φ_ij from X's own projections — ℛ is an extent-bound
 operator throughout. So **E(X) = |ℛ(X)| − |X| is the price of describing a set by its extent rather
 than by its law**: the count of what the pattern admits and the law does not. E(X) = 0 says the two
 coincide — the extent *is* the law for that set, which is P1's self-reference stated as an arithmetic
 rather than a property. Register 325.

### 12.11.4 Precision is path-dependent; physics is not
 The exact J-set of a channel is the same whether J is reached through K or directly — recoupling,
 12 of 12 (J_c, f) pairs — but the envelopes differ: 64.4% through K, 39.4% direct. The envelope does
 not commute with recoupling. The index remembers the route; the atom does not.

### 12.11.5 The shape survives, and it has a boundary
 Every stage of the tower factorises exactly over the transfer: sections 815 · 3,260 · 6,150 · 3,360 at
 Λ₁₁, 11,470 · 45,880 · 89,700 · 52,080 at Λ₁₃, log-concave, unimodal, peak at q = 2, Σ_q |A(q)|·|B(q)|
 equal to the direct count at every stage with zero defect. The object is still a cylinder — because
 every coupling axis hangs off one side of the tree. The mean transfer rises, ⟨q⟩ = 1.4631 → 1.887,
 as coupling multiplicity re-weights the profile.

 Figure 7.5. The solid in silhouette: plan (parent) and side (target) views at ±√-cell scale, Λ₁₃ filled against Λ₈
 dashed. The parent side thins toward q = 3 while the target side thickens — §12.8.1's trade, seen as shape, at both
 scales of the tower.

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"#!/bin/bash
# open58.sh -- THE OPEN, CONDENSED.  s58, on M's ruling.
#
# THE RULE THIS ENCODES:
#   ACCEPT THE HANDOFF AS SEALED.  PICK UP WHERE THE LAST SESSION ENDED.
#   DO NOT RE-PROVE THE CHAIN AT EVERY OPEN.
#
# What s57's open did, and what it cost, every session:
#     manifest verify        1140 files, both halves
#     smoke gates            13 serial, incl. nlguard 94s + gate7980 23s
#     full replay 1..71      ~3 min detached + poll cycles
#   The replay and the manifest are REDUNDANT WITH EACH OTHER.  Identical bytes
#   plus deterministic code give identical output; the hash already proved the
#   bytes.  The replay's only unique job -- catching compiler/interpreter drift --
#   is done by ONE canary in ~1 s.
#
# What this does instead:
#     STEP 1  seal      current manifest only.  History lives in LINEAGE.txt.
#     STEP 2  runtime   rebuild rt/ from sealed packs.
#     STEP 3  canary    environment drift, ~1 s.
#   Total: seconds, not minutes.  The full replay runs ONCE, at SEAL time
#   (pack58/seal58.sh), where it belongs -- proving what is being handed over,
#   not re-proving what was already handed over.
#
# ESCALATION: if the canary reports DRIFT, and only then, run the full replay.
set -u
FAIL(){ echo; echo "!!! OPEN HALTED: $1"; echo "Fix before any work."; exit 1; }
N=$(ls -d pack* 2>/dev/null | sed 's/pack//' | sort -n | tail -1)

echo "=== STEP 1 · SEAL (current only) ================================="
python3 pack58/condense.py ${N} --check || FAIL "seal check failed"

echo "=== STEP 2 · RUNTIME ============================================="
if [ ! -f rt/nlchain.jsonl ]; then
  mkdir -p rt && cp -r pack5/. rt/ && cp pack7/pack5/*.py rt/ && cp -r pack8/pack5fix/. rt/
  cp pack9/*.py pack9/*.jsonl rt/ && cp pack10/* rt/ && cp pack12/*.py pack13/*.py rt/
  cp pack16/*.py pack16/*.jsonl rt/ && cp pack17/*.py pack17/*.jsonl pack17/*.c rt/
  cp pack18/*.py pack18/*.jsonl pack18/*.c rt/
  for n in $(seq 19 $N); do for e in py jsonl c json sh; do ls pack$n/*.$e >/dev/null 2>&1 && cp pack$n/*.$e rt/; done; done
  ( cd rt && for k in shoot shoot_sr shoot_x; do gcc -O2 -shared -fPIC -o lib$k.so $k.c || exit 1; done ) \
    || FAIL "kernel compile failed"
fi
[ -f rt/prime.py ] && [ -f rt/run.sh ] || FAIL "prime.py / run.sh missing"
( cd rt && python3 prime.py 2>&1 | tail -3 )

echo "=== STEP 3 · CANARY (environment drift) =========================="
python3 pack58/canary.py || FAIL "environment drift -- NOW run pack55/gates_run55.sh 1 71"

echo
echo "=== OPEN COMPLETE ================================================"
echo "  The chain is sealed and the environment reproduces it."
echo "  Do NOT re-verify history. Work list is §6 of the s58 bridge."
echo
echo "  STANDING (s58):"
echo "    * Seal:     python3 pack58/condense.py N --seal   (never sed a verify script)"
echo "    * Retire:   undeclared removals HALT the seal. Declare in pack<N>/RETIRE.txt."
echo "    * Surveys:  counts, sets, diffs -- pack57/rd.py. Never a row dump."
echo "    * Replay:   at SEAL time only, or when the canary reports DRIFT."
","stderr":""}

{"returncode":0,"stdout":""""o89seg.py -- s77. ZENO-SEGMENTED phase O: ONE guarded solve per invocation.
Detached jobs do not survive a tool-call boundary in this container (observed at s77),
so the run is segmented instead. THE RULING PATH IS UNTOUCHED: the candidate list, the
reference and every solve go through nlchain's own helpers and NG.run_guarded.
    python3 ../pack77/o89seg.py <Z> <seed> next     # do the next unfinished item, exit
    python3 ../pack77/o89seg.py <Z> <seed> list     # what is done, what remains
Receipts append to ../pack77/o89_<Z>_<seed>.jsonl. Resume is from the receipt file (F53.3).
"""
import sys, os, json, time
os.environ.setdefault("SIC_NOCLAMP", "1"); os.environ.setdefault("SUBCELL", "1")
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
import seedtest as ST          # sealed instrument: seeds + install()
import nlchain as NC
import nlguard as NG

Z, seed, cmd = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
REC = f"../pack77/o89_{Z}_{seed}.jsonl"

rows = NC.load()
cfg_prev = NC.cfg_from_chain(Z - 1, rows)
items = ["ref"] + [NC.tagof(c) for c in NC.candidates(cfg_prev)]
cmap = {NC.tagof(c): c for c in NC.candidates(cfg_prev)}

done = {}
if os.path.exists(REC):
    for ln in open(REC):
        if ln.strip():
            r = json.loads(ln); done[r["item"]] = r
todo = [i for i in items if i not in done]

if cmd == "list":
    print(f"Z={Z} seed={seed}  {len(done)}/{len(items)} done   remaining: {' '.join(todo) or 'NONE'}")
    sys.exit(0)

if not todo:
    print(f"Z={Z} seed={seed}: COMPLETE {len(done)}/{len(items)}"); sys.exit(0)

it = todo[0]
ST.install(seed)                                   # the ONLY variable
cfg = cfg_prev if it == "ref" else NC.add(cfg_prev, cmap[it])
t0 = time.time()
g = NG.run_guarded(Z, cfg, it)
r = dict(item=it, Z=Z, seed=seed, E=g["E"], it_n=g["it"], rung=g["rung"],
         conv=g["conv"], err=g["err"], sec=int(time.time() - t0))
with open(REC, "a") as f:
    f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
print(f"  {it:>3}  E={r['E']}  it={r['it_n']}  rung={r['rung']}  conv={r['conv']}  {r['sec']}s"
      f"   [{len(done)+1}/{len(items)}]")
","stderr":""}

---

## THE STANDING POSITION, AS S79 LEFT IT

**Held:** the fixed-field inequality is computed at Z=89 — eps₃^{l=3} − eps₄^{l=2} = **+155.369 mHa** in one field, with relaxation measured at **10.072 mHa and closing the gap**. That is a measurement, not a derivation, and s79 says so in its own text.

**Open, and owed against a written result:** **F79.2**. The Z=89 margin table compares one-electron eigenvalues against total-energy differences. Measured offset at 6d is 19.277 mHa against a margin of 32.330 mHa. Every stated *multiple of the margin* is withdrawn; the qualitative verdict survives provisionally on a one-channel offset estimate that is not a bound.

---

## RECONNAISSANCE FOR ITEM 1 — DONE BEFORE ASKING FOR THE RULING

The repair is buildable. `t7e_probe.make_shoot` returns `u` as well as `nd`/`nrm`, so a node-targeted fallback can return solve_one's full contract rather than raising as `refine79` does. The five sealed Z=89 failures are all RuntimeError node-count raises at 3–4 s each, so a converged run is minutes, not hours.

**One hazard I want on the record before anything is built:** `refine79`'s scan bounds are hardcoded from the s77 windows, which describe the field at *one* iteration. A fallback living inside a live SCF sees the field move under it every iteration. An instrument that reports "no zero at target node count" when its own scan bound was too narrow is exactly F79.1's shape — and s79 already caught that once, in code written that session, only because a prediction was filed first. The scan bound must be adaptive and declared, and the prediction must say what it expects before the bound is chosen.

---

## AWAITING YOUR RULING — SCOPE FOR S80

The s79 order proposes, in order:

1. **F79.2's currency repair** — Z=89 SCF at cfg+6f/7f/8f with node-targeted fallback, report dE against −25694.384010, then restate the item-2 margins in dE. Owed against a result already written down.
2. **O-C1's falsifier** — perturb a converged Z=89 6d solution, re-converge. Cheap, never run, load-bearing since Step 0(ii) was adopted.
3. **Fixed-field comparison at a second row**, Z=90 the strongest candidate.

My recommendation is **1, then 2** — item 1 because a withdrawn claim sitting in the record is the most expensive thing here, item 2 because it is cheap and currently the only thing standing between a four-start basin test and a claim the adopted rule cannot support.

Item 3 buys a second Z but does not close anything already owed.

Your ruling on scope, and I file the prediction before any run.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""de80.py -- SESSION 80, ITEM 1.  F79.2's REPAIR.

F79.2: the Z=89 margin table compares ONE-ELECTRON EIGENVALUES against TOTAL-ENERGY
DIFFERENCES.  The repair is to obtain the f channels in the currency the ranking is
actually in: dE = E(cfg + channel) - E(ref), E(ref) = -25694.384010 (pack77/o89_89_A.jsonl).

s79's refine79.py PROVED the target-node state exists and located it, then RAISED.
This instrument does the one thing more: it RETURNS that state to the SCF, so the
field can converge on it and a TOTAL ENERGY exists to difference.

import os, sys, math, json, time, hashlib

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CACHE = os.path.join(HERE, 'de80.jsonl')
FBLOG = os.path.join(HERE, 'de80_fallback.jsonl')
PRED = os.path.join(HERE, 'PREDICTION-S80-ITEM1-CURRENCY.md')
PSHA = os.path.join(HERE, 'PREDICTION-S80-ITEM1-CURRENCY.sha256')

os.environ.setdefault("SIC_NOCLAMP", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("SUBCELL", "1")
import numpy as np
import hfc2
from t7c_kernel import C0

# ---- sealed comparands, pack77/o89_89_A.jsonl.  READ, never recomputed here.
E_REF = -25694.38401018016
SEALED_E = {'6d': -25694.541630577907, '7p': -25694.509298091765,
            '5f': -25694.41547324462}
NL = {'6f': (6, 3), '7f': (7, 3), '8f': (8, 3), '6d': (6, 2), '7p': (7, 1), '5f': (5, 3)}

NSCAN = 400          # G2
SLO, SHI = 0.20, 8.0  # G2: window = [SLO,SHI] x |e_returned|
NARROW = (0.55, 1.8)  # G3
EDGEFRAC = 0.05      # G2: a zero this close to an edge is flagged


def gate_sha():
    """R 1449: the driver halts unless the filed prediction is intact."""
    want = open(PSHA).read().strip().split()[0]
    got = hashlib.sha256(open(PRED, 'rb').read()).hexdigest()
    if want != got:
        raise SystemExit(f"HALT: prediction sha mismatch\n  filed {want}\n  now   {got}")
    return got


class Fallback(hfc2.HFC):
    """Inert on healthy channels.  On nd != n-l-1, returns the TARGET-node state."""
    FORCE = None          # G4
    LOG = None            # list, appended per fallback firing
    LAST = {}             # G3: channel -> previous zero

    def _scan(self, sh, tgt, lo_e, hi_e, npts):
        es = -np.geomspace(abs(lo_e), abs(hi_e), npts)
        win = []
        for ee in es:
            o = sh(float(ee))
            if o is None:
                continue
            if o['nd'] == tgt:
                win.append((float(ee), math.log(max(o['nrm'], 1e-300))))
        sc = [k for k in range(len(win) - 1) if (win[k][1] > 0) != (win[k + 1][1] > 0)]
        if not sc:
            return None, win
        a, b = win[sc[0]][0], win[sc[0] + 1][0]
        fa = win[sc[0]][1]
        for _ in range(80):
            m = 0.5 * (a + b)
            o = sh(float(m))
            if o is None:
                break
            fm = math.log(max(o['nrm'], 1e-300))
            if abs(fm) < 1e-11 or abs(b - a) < 1e-14:
                a = b = m
                break
            if (fm > 0) == (fa > 0):
                a, fa = m, fm
            else:
                b = m
        return 0.5 * (a + b), win

    def solve_one(self, l, n, Vloc, X, e0, Pold=None):
        u, e, nd, res = super().solve_one(l, n, Vloc, X, e0, Pold)
        ch = f"{n}{'spdfg'[l]}"
        tgt = n - l - 1
        if nd == tgt and ch != self.FORCE:
            return u, e, nd, res                      # INERT -- ruling path untouched
        import t7e_probe as P
        cap = dict(l=l, n=n, Vloc=np.array(Vloc, float), X=np.array(X, float), Pold=Pold,
                   r=self.r, x=self.x, h=self.h, dr=self.dr, N=self.npts, c=self.c,
                   srcM=self.srcM, Z=self.Z)
        sh = P.make_shoot(cap)

        base = abs(float(e))
        mode = 'wide'
        z = None
        prev = self.LAST.get(ch)
        if prev is not None:                          # G3: narrow first, cost only
            z, win = self._scan(sh, tgt, -NARROW[0] * abs(prev), -NARROW[1] * abs(prev),

            if z is not None:
                mode = 'narrow'
                lo_e, hi_e = -NARROW[0] * abs(prev), -NARROW[1] * abs(prev)
        if z is None:                                 # G3: wide always available
            lo_e, hi_e = -SLO * base, -SHI * base
            z, win = self._scan(sh, tgt, lo_e, hi_e, NSCAN)
            mode = 'wide'
        if z is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Z={self.Z} {ch} FALLBACK FOUND NO TARGET-NODE ZERO "
                               f"in [{lo_e:.6g},{hi_e:.6g}] tgt={tgt} nd={nd}")

        o = sh(float(z))
        span = math.log(abs(hi_e) / abs(lo_e))
        d_lo = math.log(abs(z) / abs(lo_e)) / span
        d_hi = math.log(abs(hi_e) / abs(z)) / span
        if self.LOG is not None:
            self.LOG.append(dict(ch=ch, tgt=tgt, nd_std=int(nd), e_std=round(float(e), 9),
                                 e_fb=round(float(z), 9), nd_fb=int(o['nd']),
                                 logn=round(math.log(max(o['nrm'], 1e-300)), 6),
                                 mode=mode, win_pts=len(win),
                                 scan=[round(lo_e, 8), round(hi_e, 8)],
                                 edge_lo=bool(d_lo < EDGEFRAC), edge_hi=bool(d_hi < EDGEFRAC),
                                 forced=bool(ch == self.FORCE)))
        self.LAST[ch] = z
        nrm = float(o['nrm'])
        return o['u'] / math.sqrt(nrm), float(z), int(o['nd']), abs(math.log(nrm))


def guarded(Z, cfg, force=None):
    """G5: nlguard.LADDER, replicated verbatim.  Only the class differs."""
    import nlguard as NG
    last = None
    for rung, (beta, maxit) in enumerate(NG.LADDER):
        t = time.time()
        Fallback.FORCE = force
        Fallback.LOG = []
        Fallback.LAST = {}
        try:
            E, _, it, eps = Fallback(Z, [tuple(x) for x in cfg], c=C0).run2(
                beta=beta, maxit=maxit)
        except Exception as e:
            return dict(E=None, it=None, beta=beta, rung=rung, conv=False,
                        err=type(e).__name__ + ": " + str(e)[:160],
                        sec=int(time.time() - t), fb=Fallback.LOG)
        if it < maxit:
            return dict(E=float(E), it=it, beta=beta, rung=rung, conv=True, err=None,
                        sec=int(time.time() - t), fb=Fallback.LOG,
                        eps={f"{k[0]}{'spdfg'[k[1]]}": round(float(v), 9)
                             for k, v in eps.items()})
        last = (E, it, beta, maxit)

    return dict(E=None, it=it, beta=beta, rung=len(NG.LADDER) - 1, conv=False,

def put(rec):
    with open(CACHE, 'a') as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(rec) + '\n')


def cfgs(ch):
    import nlchain as NC
    rows = NC.load()
    cfg = NC.cfg_from_chain(88, rows)
    return NC.add(cfg, NL[ch])


def verdict(dE, baseline_dE):
    """G5: BOTH verdicts must be reachable.  Returns the entrant question's answer."""
    return "ENTRANT CHANGES" if dE < baseline_dE else "ROW HOLDS"


def run(ch, force=None, tag=None):
    gate_sha()
    t0 = time.time()
    g = guarded(89, cfgs(ch), force=force)
    dE = None if g['E'] is None else g['E'] - E_REF
    rec = dict(kind=(tag or 'question'), ch=ch, Z=89, forced=force,
               E=g['E'], dE=(None if dE is None else round(dE, 9)),
               it=g['it'], rung=g['rung'], conv=g['conv'], err=g['err'],
               n_fb=len(g['fb']), sec=int(time.time() - t0),
               eps_ch=(g.get('eps') or {}).get(ch),
               edge_flags=sum(1 for f in g['fb'] if f['edge_lo'] or f['edge_hi']),
               fb_first=(g['fb'][0] if g['fb'] else None),
               fb_last=(g['fb'][-1] if g['fb'] else None))
    put(rec)
    with open(FBLOG, 'a') as f:
        for x in g['fb']:
            f.write(json.dumps(dict(kind=rec['kind'], ch=ch, **x)) + '\n')
    print(f"  Z=89 {ch:>3} [{rec['kind']}] E={rec['E']}  dE={rec['dE']}  "
          f"it={rec['it']} rung={rec['rung']} conv={rec['conv']}  "
          f"fb={rec['n_fb']} edge={rec['edge_flags']}  {rec['sec']}s")
    if rec['err']:
        print(f"    err={rec['err']}")
    if rec['fb_last']:
        x = rec['fb_last']
        print(f"    last fallback: e_std={x['e_std']} -> e_fb={x['e_fb']} "
              f"nd {x['nd_std']}->{x['nd_fb']} logn={x['logn']} mode={x['mode']} "
              f"edge=({x['edge_lo']},{x['edge_hi']})")
    return rec


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cmd = sys.argv[1]
    if cmd == 'control-machinery':
        r = run('6d', force=None, tag='C1')
        want = SEALED_E['6d']
        ok = r['E'] is not None and abs(r['E'] - want) < 1e-9
        print(f"  C1 sealed {want}  got {r['E']}  -> {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    elif cmd == 'control-fallback':
        r = run('6d', force='6d', tag='C2')
        want = SEALED_E['6d']
        ok = r['E'] is not None and abs(r['E'] - want) < 1e-6 and r['n_fb'] > 0
        print(f"  C2 sealed {want}  got {r['E']}  fired {r['n_fb']}x  "
              f"-> {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    elif cmd == 'control-scorer':
        gate_sha()
        d6d = SEALED_E['6d'] - E_REF
        d7p = SEALED_E['7p'] - E_REF
        d5f = SEALED_E['5f'] - E_REF
        a = verdict(d6d, d7p)
        b = verdict(d5f, d6d)
        print(f"  C3 direction A: 6d dE={d6d:.6f} vs baseline 7p dE={d7p:.6f} -> {a}")
        print(f"  C3 direction B: 5f dE={d5f:.6f} vs baseline 6d dE={d6d:.6f} -> {b}")
        ok = (a == "ENTRANT CHANGES") and (b == "ROW HOLDS")
        print(f"  C3 both verdicts reachable -> {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    elif cmd == 'run':
        run(sys.argv[2])
    elif cmd == 'score':
        gate_sha()
        import subprocess
        rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(CACHE)]
        q = {r['ch']: r for r in rows if r['kind'] == 'question'}
        d6d = SEALED_E['6d'] - E_REF
        d7p = SEALED_E['7p'] - E_REF
        m = d7p - d6d
        print(f"  baseline: 6d dE={d6d*1000:.3f} mHa (rank 1), 7p dE={d7p*1000:.3f} mHa "
              f"(rank 2), m(89)={m*1000:.3f} mHa")
        print(f"  {'ch':>4} {'dE (mHa)':>12} {'above 6d':>12} {'above 7p':>12} "
              f"{'x m':>8}  verdict")
        for ch in ('6f', '7f', '8f'):
            if ch not in q or q[ch]['dE'] is None:
                print(f"  {ch:>4}  NOT CONVERGED")
                continue
            d = q[ch]['dE']
            print(f"  {ch:>4} {d*1000:12.3f} {(d-d6d)*1000:12.3f} {(d-d7p)*1000:12.3f} "
                  f"{(d-d7p)/m:8.3f}  {verdict(d, d7p)}")

content.text:
**STOP — a fault, and it is material.** The fallback fired once and found the zero at −0.020040. `refine79` found −0.031600 for the same channel. Both are target-node zeros of the same field; s79 recorded `sign_changes = 2` and left it undiagnosed.

The difference is scan *orientation*. `refine79` scans most-bound-first and takes the first crossing; my `_scan` builds `geomspace` in the opposite direction and so takes the other zero. Neither instrument declared its orientation. This is the same species as F79.1 and F79.2 — a number carried under a name that does not describe it.

Registering it and repairing before anything is scored.

input.new_str:
def _bisect(self, sh, a, b, fa):
        for _ in range(80):
            m = 0.5 * (a + b)
            o = sh(float(m))
            if o is None:
                break
            fm = math.log(max(o['nrm'], 1e-300))
            if abs(fm) < 1e-11 or abs(b - a) < 1e-14:
                a = b = m
                break
            if (fm > 0) == (fa > 0):
                a, fa = m, fm
            else:
                b = m
        return 0.5 * (a + b)

    def _scan(self, sh, tgt, lo_e, hi_e, npts):
        """G6.  EVERY crossing is bisected, not the first.

        s79 left `sign_changes = 2` undiagnosed and both instruments silently took
        ONE of the two zeros -- refine79 the more bound, this instrument's first
        draft the less bound, purely because their geomspace arguments ran in
        opposite directions.  NEITHER DECLARED AN ORIENTATION.  That is F80.1.
        The repair is not to pick better: it is to RETURN THE WHOLE ZERO SET, so the
        selection is a declared act on a recorded spread rather than an accident of
        argument order.  ZEROS ARE RETURNED MOST-BOUND FIRST, ALWAYS.
        """
        es = -np.geomspace(abs(lo_e), abs(hi_e), npts)      # ascending |e|
        win = []
        for ee in es:
            o = sh(float(ee))
            if o is None:
                continue
            if o['nd'] == tgt:
                win.append((float(ee), math.log(max(o['nrm'], 1e-300))))
        sc = [k for k in range(len(win) - 1) if (win[k][1] > 0) != (win[k + 1][1] > 0)]
        zs = [self._bisect(sh, win[k][0], win[k + 1][0], win[k][1]) for k in sc]
        zs.sort()                                            # most bound first
        return zs, win

input.file_text:
# F80.1 — WHEN THE TARGET-NODE ZERO SET HAS TWO MEMBERS, BOTH s79's INSTRUMENT AND THIS
# ONE SELECTED SILENTLY, BY THE ORDER OF THEIR OWN geomspace ARGUMENTS. THEY SELECTED
# OPPOSITE MEMBERS. SEVERITY: THE SELECTED STATE DECIDES THE ANSWER.
# RAISED AND CLOSED IN THIS SESSION, ON THE SELF-CONSISTENCY CRITERION.

## THE UNDIAGNOSED FACT s79 LEFT ON THE TABLE
pack79/RESULT-S79-ITEM2 recorded `sign_changes = 2` on all three f channels and filed it
as *"undiagnosed"*: two energies carrying the target node count with nrm = 1. It then
stated that refine79 *"bisects the FIRST, which is the more bound"*, and reasoned that
taking the more bound made the conclusion conservative.

## WHAT WAS NOT SEEN: "FIRST" IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE FIELD
refine79 builds `es = -geomspace(abs(lo_e), abs(hi_e))` with `lo_e = win[0]*PAD` — the
MORE bound end — so its scan runs most-bound to least-bound and its first crossing is the
MORE bound zero. de80's first draft built the same expression with the arguments in the
opposite order, so its first crossing was the LESS bound zero. **Neither instrument
declared an orientation. The two differ at 6f by 11.6 mHa, and the choice was made by
argument order, not by any stated rule.**

## THE REPAIR, DECLARED AS G6 AND G7
G6: every crossing is bisected, not the first; the scan returns the WHOLE zero set,
sorted most-bound first, and `n_zeros` and `spread` are recorded on every firing.
G7: selection is an explicit argument, `most-bound` or `least-bound`, and **BOTH WERE
RUN.** Method §2.24: a single heuristic cannot tell you whether you are in the case where
it works — run two and report the SPREAD.

## THE SPREAD, AND IT IS NOT A SPREAD — IT IS A DISQUALIFICATION
| ch | most-bound | least-bound |
|---|---|---|
| 6f | **NO SCF.** RuntimeError node count, fb=7 on the wide window | conv, 83 it, dE = **-0.020486** |
| 7f | **NO SCF.** RuntimeError node count, fb=3 | conv, 86 it, dE = **-0.014282** |
| 8f | **NO SCF.** the target-node zero set becomes EMPTY as the field drifts | conv, 85 it, dE = **-0.010528** |
**The more-bound branch does not support a self-consistent field at any of the three
channels. The less-bound branch converges at all three, in one fallback firing.**
The most-bound failure was re-run with the G3 warm start DISABLED and fails identically,
so it is not an artefact of the narrow window. **The instrument REFUSES rather than
coerces (§2.9): it returns a state whose node count is not the target and run2 raises.**

## AND s79's OWN FLAGGED ANOMALY IS THE SYMPTOM, NOW RESOLVED
s79 recorded, not buried: *"6f AT -0.031600 IS 0.140 mHa MORE BOUND THAN SEALED 5f AT
-0.03146. Within one fixed field min-max forbids that ordering."* It was excused because
the two are different SCF fields. **On the surviving branch the anomaly does not arise:
6f dE = -0.020486 is 10.98 mHa LESS bound than 5f dE = -0.031463, which is the ordering
min-max wants.** The flag was pointing at the selection, and it was right.

## WHAT IS WITHDRAWN
**pack79's three f eigenvalues — -0.031600440, -0.020275522, -0.014084998 — are the
MORE-BOUND branch and are withdrawn as descriptions of the 6f/7f/8f states of the
self-consistent field.** They remain correct as what they were measured to be: zeros of
log(nrm) at the target node count in the iteration-1 field. **They are not the states the
field converges on.** Every margin s79 computed from them is superseded by §the result.
s79's item-2 verdict — entrant unchanged, ranks 1 and 2 untouched — SURVIVES, and is
now carried by dE rather than by eigenvalues.

## THE SPECIES, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE AGAIN
F78.1: read the raise, not the sentence. F79.1: read the instrument, not the label on its
output column. F79.2: read the units. **F80.1: READ WHICH ONE IT PICKED, AND WHY.** Four
faults in three sessions, one species — a number carried forward under a name that did not
describe it. **Here the name was "the" target-node zero, and there were two.**

## TIMING FLAG, DECLARED
**G6 and G7 were written AFTER the first 6f run returned a zero that disagreed with
refine79's.** The design decision followed a numerical result and is flagged as such. The
prediction file was NOT edited; its sha gate held across the amendment, and C2 was
re-run against the amended code path and passed before any question run was scored.

# RESULT S80 — ITEM 1. F79.2 IS CLOSED. THE Z=89 TABLE IS NOW IN ONE CURRENCY.
# THE ENTRANT IS UNCHANGED AND THE MARGINS ARE LARGER, NOT SMALLER, THAN THE WITHDRAWN ONES.
# Prediction sha256 560ce4ad3c2be891fd4bac5ce72fddbc10810100e986547d10a94a443839a641, filed first.
# Instrument pack80/de80.py — SEVEN declared lines from sealed hfc2.py / nlguard.py.

## THE THREE CAN-FAILS, RUN FIRST, ALL PASSED, AND ONE OF THEM IS NEW TO THIS PROJECT
C3 SCORER — 6d against baseline 7p returns **ENTRANT CHANGES**; 5f against baseline 6d
   returns **ROW HOLDS**. M's order required an instrument whose verdict space is not
   one-sided. Both verdicts reachable on the identical path.
C1 MACHINERY — 6d with the fallback INERT returns **E = -25694.541630577907, the sealed
   pack77 value to every digit**, 44 iterations, and **fb = 0**: the fallback does not
   touch the ruling path on a healthy channel.
C2 FALLBACK PATH — 6d with the fallback **FORCED** on the 6d channel fires on all 44
   iterations, returns **e_fb = e_std = -0.176897462, identical to nine digits**, and
   lands on **-25694.541630579646, the sealed energy to 1.7e-9.**
   **THIS IS THE CONTROL s79 DID NOT HAVE.** refine79 could show a state existed; it
   could not show that RETURNING that state reproduces what the ruling path returns.

## THE MEASUREMENT — dE = E(cfg88 + ch) - E(ref), E(ref) = -25694.38401018016
| ch | E | dE (mHa) | above 6d | above 7p | x m(89) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **6f** | -25694.404496178428 | **-20.486** | 137.134 | **104.802** | **3.241** | ROW HOLDS |
| **7f** | -25694.398292407324 | **-14.282** | 143.338 | **111.006** | **3.433** | ROW HOLDS |
| **8f** | -25694.394538374345 | **-10.528** | 147.092 | **114.760** | **3.549** | ROW HOLDS |
Baselines, sealed: 6d dE = **-157.620** (rank 1), 7p dE = **-125.288** (rank 2),
m(89) = **32.332 mHa**. All three converged at rung 0, 83-86 iterations, **zero edge flags**.
**THE ENTRANT AT Z=89 IS 6d. NEITHER RANK 1 NOR RANK 2 IS TOUCHED, AND THE MULTIPLES OF
THE MARGIN ARE NOW RATIOS OF LIKE QUANTITIES AND MAY BE STATED.**

## F79.2 IS CLOSED
The withdrawn multiples are superseded, not restored: **2.898 m -> 3.241 m, 3.248 m ->
3.433 m, 3.440 m -> 3.549 m.** The repair moved every f channel FURTHER from rank 2, by
11.1, 6.0 and 3.6 mHa. **The Z=89 hole is no longer three eigenvalues and two brackets.
It is three converged rows in the table that decides the row.** Two brackets — 7d and
8d — remain, and are untouched by this session.

## THE CURRENCY OFFSET, NOW MEASURED AT FOUR CHANNELS INSTEAD OF ONE
| ch | dE | eps (converged) | dE - eps |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6d | -0.157620 | -0.176898 | **+19.277 mHa** |
| 6f | -0.020486 | -0.020354 | **-0.132 mHa** |
| 7f | -0.014282 | -0.014151 | **-0.132 mHa** |
| 8f | -0.010528 | -0.010393 | **-0.135 mHa** |
**THE OFFSET IS 146 TIMES SMALLER AT THE f CHANNELS THAN AT 6d, AND IT IS OF THE
OPPOSITE SIGN.** F79.2 warned that the one-channel 6d offset was *"an estimate from one
channel's offset, NOT a bound on the offset in the others."* That warning was correct and
is now discharged by measurement: the offset does not transfer between channels.
**This is why the repair had to be run rather than argued.**

## PREDICTION SCORED — X2 X3 X6 X7 CORRECT, X1 SPLIT, X4 AND X5 FALSIFIED
  X1 all three converge . . . . **SPLIT.** True on the surviving branch; FALSE on the
     other, and the prediction did not know a branch choice existed. See F80.1.
  X2 entrant unchanged, all above 6d AND above 7p . . **CORRECT**, 137-147 mHa above 6d.
  X3 dE ordering matches eigenvalue ordering . . **CORRECT** — and this was filed as
     *"the clause most likely to fail... I expect it to be the one that costs me."*
     It did not. **The clause I trusted least held; two I did not flag broke.**
  X4 offset positive and under 19.277 mHa . . **FALSIFIED ON SIGN.** It is NEGATIVE,
     -0.13 mHa. The magnitude clause was right and the reasoning behind it — a diffuse f
     orbital perturbs the [Rn] core less — survives; **the sign was asserted from one
     channel's example and was wrong.**
  X5 the fallback fires on every iteration, n_fb == it . . **FALSIFIED, AND BADLY.**
     **n_fb = 1 on all three.** The fallback fires ONCE, on iteration 1, and every channel
     is healthy for the remaining 82-85 iterations. **The filed rationale — that state
     misidentification is structural because eigen_sr's guess carries no knowledge of the
     node count — is WRONG. It is a START-UP ARTEFACT.** Once the SCF is placed on the
     correct state it stays there of its own accord. This is a fact about the field, it
     was not predicted, and it is the most interesting thing in the run.
  X6 no scan-bound edge flag . . **CORRECT** — zero flags on any converged channel.
  X7 margins larger than the withdrawn ones by under 20 mHa . **CORRECT** — +11.1, +6.0,
     +3.6 mHa. Recorded: the withdrawn figures were computed from the branch F80.1
     rejects, so this clause is scored against superseded numbers.

## RECORDED AGAINST THIS RESULT, NOT BURIED
1. **F80.1 IS RAISED AGAINST THIS SESSION'S OWN FIRST RUN**, and the instrument was
   amended after a numerical result. Timing flag declared in F80.1.
2. **ONE SEED, SEED A's CHAIN.** The reference and the two baselines are sealed seed-A
   values. Nothing here re-seeds.
3. **THE FALLBACK IS NOT A PROOF THAT THE FIELD HAS NO OTHER SOLUTION.** It shows the
   more-bound branch does not self-consistently close and the less-bound branch does.
   That is a statement about what the program reaches, which is O-C1's territory.
4. **THIS IS A RANKING RESULT, NOT A DERIVATION.** It closes a fault against a written
   result. It derives no property of F_core and must never be quoted as doing so.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""perturb80.py -- SESSION 80, ITEM 2.  O-C1's FALSIFIER.

Step 0(ii) was ADOPTED at s79: the field is DEFINED as a GLOBAL MINIMISER of E^RHF at
fixed shell occupancies.  RULING-S79 registered the obligation and named the falsifier:
    "THE FALSIFIER IS CHEAP AND IS NOT YET RUN: perturb a CONVERGED solution and
     re-converge.  A second basin at lower energy kills the rule as stated."
The evidence held is four seeds agreeing from 52 Ha away.  s79 wrote: "THAT IS A
FOUR-START BASIN TEST.  IT IS NOT A PROOF OF A GLOBAL MINIMUM."  Seeds probe where the
iteration STARTS.  This probes the neighbourhood of where it LANDS, which is the
different question, and the one O-C1 actually asks.

DECLARED LINES FROM THE SEALED PATH:
  H1  hfc2.HFC.seed is overridden to return a PERTURBED COPY of a stored converged
      solution instead of the numerov seed.  run2, solve_one, the field and the energy
      functional are UNTOUCHED.
  H2  THE LEVER IS VERIFIED ON EVERY RUN, NOT ONCE.  The standing methodological law
      (F54.2): an instrument that varies a parameter must DEMONSTRATE the parameter
      moves the object before any row is computed.  Each run reports dP = max over
      shells of ||P_pert - P*||_2.  amp > 0 with dP = 0 EXITS rc=4 and computes nothing.
  H3  TWO KINDS OF PERTURBATION, not one (Method 2.24).  'noise' is isotropic and
      structureless; 'mix' contaminates each shell with the next shell of the same l,
      which is the direction an RHF instability would actually lie along.  A basin that
      survives only one kind has not been tested.
  H4  THE COMPARATOR REPORTS THREE VERDICTS, and the lower-energy one is the kill.
      SAME BASIN | SECOND BASIN, LOWER -- O-C1 FALSIFIED | SECOND SOLUTION, HIGHER.

usage:  python3 perturb80.py control-return     # comparator can say SAME
        python3 perturb80.py control-differ     # comparator can say NOT SAME
        python3 perturb80.py run <kind> <amp> <rng>
        python3 perturb80.py score
"""
import os, sys, math, json, time, hashlib

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CACHE = os.path.join(HERE, 'perturb80.jsonl')
PRED = os.path.join(HERE, 'PREDICTION-S80-ITEM2-OC1.md')
PSHA = os.path.join(HERE, 'PREDICTION-S80-ITEM2-OC1.sha256')

os.environ.setdefault("SIC_NOCLAMP", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("SUBCELL", "1")
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
import numpy as np
import hfc2
from t7c_kernel import C0

E_SEALED_6D = -25694.541630577907
TOL = 1e-6                      # same-rung identity; F47.3's ~1e-5 is the mixed-rung figure


def gate_sha():
    want = open(PSHA).read().strip().split()[0]
    got = hashlib.sha256(open(PRED, 'rb').read()).hexdigest()
    if want != got:
        raise SystemExit(f"HALT: prediction sha mismatch\n  filed {want}\n  now   {got}")


class Perturbed(hfc2.HFC):
    """H1.  Starts from a stored converged solution, perturbed."""
    P0 = None
    EPS0 = None
    AMP = 0.0
    KIND = 'noise'
    RNG = 0
    DP = None

    def seed(self, qtail):
        dr = self.dr
        P = {k: v.copy() for k, v in self.P0.items()}
        eps = dict(self.EPS0)
        if self.AMP > 0:
            rng = np.random.default_rng(self.RNG)
            keys = list(P.keys())
            byl = {}
            for (n, l) in keys:
                byl.setdefault(l, []).append((n, l))
            for l in byl:
                byl[l].sort()
            for a in keys:
                if self.KIND == 'noise':
                    d = rng.standard_normal(self.npts) * np.abs(P[a])
                elif self.KIND == 'mix':
                    sib = byl[a[1]]
                    i = sib.index(a)
                    b = sib[(i + 1) % len(sib)]
                    d = P[b].copy() if b != a else rng.standard_normal(self.npts) * np.abs(P[a])
                else:
                    raise SystemExit(f"unknown kind {self.KIND}")
                nd_ = math.sqrt(float(np.sum(d * d * dr)))
                if nd_ > 0:
                    d = d / nd_
                P[a] = P[a] + self.AMP * d
                P[a] = P[a] / math.sqrt(float(np.sum(P[a] ** 2 * dr)))
        # H2: LEVER VERIFICATION, EVERY RUN
        self.DP = max(math.sqrt(float(np.sum((P[k] - self.P0[k]) ** 2 * dr))) for k in P)
        return P, eps


def converge_reference():
    import nlchain as NC
    rows = NC.load()
    cfg = NC.add(NC.cfg_from_chain(88, rows), (6, 2))
    h = hfc2.HFC(89, [tuple(t) for t in cfg], c=C0)
    E, Ec, it, eps = h.run2(beta=0.4, maxit=100)
    return h, cfg, float(E), it


def verdict(E, Eref):
    if E is None:
        return "NO CONVERGENCE"
    d = E - Eref
    if abs(d) <= TOL:
        return "SAME BASIN"
    if d < -TOL:
        return "SECOND BASIN, LOWER -- O-C1 FALSIFIED"
    return "SECOND SOLUTION, HIGHER"


def run(kind, amp, rngseed, maxit=100, tag=None):
    gate_sha()
    t0 = time.time()
    h, cfg, Eref, itref = converge_reference()
    if abs(Eref - E_SEALED_6D) > 1e-9:
        raise SystemExit(f"HALT: reference is not the sealed 6d solution: {Eref}")
    Perturbed.P0, Perturbed.EPS0 = h.P, h.eps
    Perturbed.AMP, Perturbed.KIND, Perturbed.RNG = float(amp), kind, int(rngseed)
    p = Perturbed(89, [tuple(t) for t in cfg], c=C0)
    err = None
    try:
        E, Ec, it, eps = p.run2(beta=0.4, maxit=maxit)
        E = float(E)
    except Exception as e:
        E, it = None, None
        err = type(e).__name__ + ": " + str(e)[:120]
    dp = p.DP
    if amp > 0 and (dp is None or dp < 1e-12):          # H2
        print(f"  LEVER DEAD: amp={amp} produced dP={dp}. NOTHING COMPUTED.")
        sys.exit(4)
    v = verdict(E, Eref)
    rec = dict(kind=(tag or 'question'), pert=kind, amp=float(amp), rng=int(rngseed),

               E_ref=Eref, E=E, dE_mHa=(None if E is None else round((E - Eref) * 1000, 6)),

Step 0(ii) was ADOPTED at s79: the field is DEFINED as a GLOBAL MINIMISER of E^RHF at
fixed shell occupancies.  RULING-S79 registered the obligation and named the falsifier:

      functional are UNTOUCHED.

      (F54.2): an instrument that varies a parameter must DEMONSTRATE the parameter
      moves the object before any row is computed.  Each run reports dP = max over
      shells of ||P_pert - P*||_2.  amp > 0 with dP = 0 EXITS rc=4 and computes nothing.
  H3  TWO KINDS OF PERTURBATION, not one (Method 2.24).  'noise' is isotropic and
      structureless; 'mix' contaminates each shell with the next shell of the same l,
      which is the direction an RHF instability would actually lie along.  A basin that
      survives only one kind has not been tested.

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

PRED = os.path.join(HERE, 'PREDICTION-S80-ITEM2-OC1.md')

import hfc2
from t7c_kernel import C0

    got = hashlib.sha256(open(PRED, 'rb').read()).hexdigest()

        raise SystemExit(f"HALT: prediction sha mismatch\n  filed {want}\n  now   {got}")


class Perturbed(hfc2.HFC):
    """H1.  Starts from a stored converged solution, perturbed."""
    P0 = None
    EPS0 = None
    AMP = 0.0
    KIND = 'noise'
    RNG = 0
    DP = None

    def seed(self, qtail):
        dr = self.dr
        P = {k: v.copy() for k, v in self.P0.items()}
        eps = dict(self.EPS0)
        if self.AMP > 0:
            rng = np.random.default_rng(self.RNG)
            keys = list(P.keys())
            byl = {}
            for (n, l) in keys:
                byl.setdefault(l, []).append((n, l))
            for l in byl:
                byl[l].sort()
            for a in keys:
                if self.KIND == 'noise':
                    d = rng.standard_normal(self.npts) * np.abs(P[a])
                elif self.KIND == 'mix':
                    sib = byl[a[1]]
                    i = sib.index(a)
                    b = sib[(i + 1) % len(sib)]
                    d = P[b].copy() if b != a else rng.standard_normal(self.npts) * np.abs(P[a])

                    raise SystemExit(f"unknown kind {self.KIND}")

                if nd_ > 0:
                    d = d / nd_

                P[a] = P[a] / math.sqrt(float(np.sum(P[a] ** 2 * dr)))

    if abs(d) <= TOL:

               it=it, err=err, verdict=v, sec=int(time.time() - t0))

        f.write(json.dumps(rec) + '\n')
    print(f"  {kind:>5} amp={amp:<5} rng={rngseed}  dP={rec['dP']}  E={E}  "
          f"dE={rec['dE_mHa']} mHa  it={it}  -> {v}   {rec['sec']}s")

## SESSION 80 SEALED — HANDOFF RECOMMENDED

**Context is at ~90%. Per the Prime Handoff Directive: open Session 81 in a new chat with `bash pack58/open58.sh` using the LOWDIN-HANDOFF-80 tar.**

Seal: **1310/1310, root `6ac374c6…471c7a`**. Fresh-extract tested with `rt/` deleted and rebuilt from packs — full open passes clean.

**Items 1 and 2 closed. Item 3 not started** — context ran out before Z=90 could begin. It carries to s81 as item 1, and it now inherits three repairs s79 did not have, so it is better placed than it would have been today.

**Item 1 — F79.2 closed.** The Z=89 table is in one currency. 6f/7f/8f come in at −20.486, −14.282, −10.528 mHa; the entrant is 6d and ranks 1 and 2 are untouched. The withdrawn multiples are superseded and *larger*: 2.898 m → 3.241 m. F79.2's warning that the 6d offset was not a bound on the others proved exactly right — the offset is +19.277 mHa at 6d and −0.13 mHa at the f channels, 146× smaller and opposite in sign. It had to be run, not argued.

**Item 2 — O-C1's falsifier run for the first time. Not falsified, and not established.** Eight perturbations returned to within 1.7 parts per billion. What is new is a **floor**: this test resolves a competing basin only below ~0.035 mHa. A bare null says nothing; a null with a measured floor says how much has been excluded.

**Three faults, all raised against this session's own work.** F80.1 diagnosed s79's undiagnosed `sign_changes = 2` — two zeros carry the target node count, neither instrument declared which it took, and the more-bound branch supports no self-consistent field at all. F80.2 was found by a can-fail that *failed*: the sealed energies sit 0.034 mHa above their own basin floor because `run2` stops on eigenvalue drift while Step 0(ii) is stated on the energy. F80.3 is against my own tolerance, which was set below the resolution F80.2 measured, so the instrument printed "O-C1 FALSIFIED" three times on its own scatter. Those labels are overridden in the record with the reason attached.

**On your reservation about Item 3:** it now looks more likely to help than it did this morning, but not for the reason either of us had. `fixed79.py` locates its zero by taking the first crossing in its own argument order — that is F80.1 exactly. Z=90 run with the unpatched instrument would have inherited the fault silently. Whatever a second Z is worth, it is worth more than it was.

**Nothing in clause 1 moved.** No property of F_core was derived, and the 10.1 mHa target stands where s79 left it.
